answer.what_it_does: Manus AI is an autonomous general AI agent designed to complete tasks and deliver finished work, not just answer questions.[3][8] It operates as a virtual colleague with planning, execution, and delivery capabilities inside a sandboxed environment with internet access, a persistent file system, and software-installation ability.[3]

facts.claim: Manus says it builds general AI agents as the 'Action Engine for life.'
Manus 2.0 includes a cascade agent harness, Cloud Computer, Automations, Manus Studio, and Cue.
Manus is available for macOS, Windows, iOS, and Android.
Manus features include building apps, creating media, researching the web, automating recurring work, and connecting tools already in use.
Manus Agent Skills are executed end-to-end in a secure sandbox environment.
Manus agents can be accessed and managed via API.

answer.what_it_does: Manus AI is an autonomous AI agent platform that executes complex, multi-step tasks independently. It runs work in a cloud virtual machine and can use tools/connectors to carry out workflows like research, content/project creation, and automation.

ai_agents.name: Manus (Autonomous Agent Platform)
ai_agents.what_it_does: Plans and executes multi-step tasks in an agent mode, including complex workflows beyond simple chat.
actions: Execute tasks using an underlying cloud virtual machine / sandbox environment for running workloads
Use agent-mode workflows for complex tasks (e.g., creating projects such as websites/slides/videos via platform features)
Run “Wide Research” via parallel processing / agent-to-agent collaboration for large information-gathering tasks
Interact with connected third-party services via connectors / integration layer (e.g., Notion MCP, Notion connector) and update external workspaces
Use “Automations” that can trigger runs from connected apps/systems (integration list includes common SaaS apps)
Use “My Computer” / Desktop capability to execute command line instructions and work with local files/apps via the desktop app

use_cases.name: Parallelized high-volume research and synthesis
use_cases.who_uses_it: Pro users / teams running research-intensive workflows
what_the_agent_can_reach: Up to hundreds of items/sources in parallel research workflows (within Manus’s environment)
Connected documentation/workspace systems used as inputs/outputs for research results (e.g., Notion pages/databases via connectors)

use_cases.name: Project-based execution with reusable instructions, files, and skills
use_cases.who_uses_it: Individuals and teams using Manus Projects
what_the_agent_can_reach: Project context artifacts (instructions, files/sources) stored within Manus project workspaces
Connected tools (examples listed include Gmail/Google/Slack/GitHub within Teams/Projects positioning) depending on user authorization
Team collaboration spaces and shared project context (collaboration permissions controlled by the team/workspace)

use_cases.name: Notion knowledge/workflow automation (read/update/write)
use_cases.who_uses_it: Teams using Notion as a project tracker or knowledge base
what_the_agent_can_reach: Notion pages and databases (read/search; create; update properties and comments)
Notion project management artifacts such as task statuses/owners/due dates and weekly report pages
Scheduled/triggered automations tied to Notion connector actions

use_cases.name: Scheduled or event-driven automations across SaaS tools
use_cases.who_uses_it: Teams building recurring workflows with Manus Automations
what_the_agent_can_reach: Trigger events from connected apps (Apps list includes Gmail, Outlook, Google Calendar, GitHub, Shopify, Slack, Notion, RSS, and Webhook—depending on user connections/authorizations)
Webhook targets configured by users for workflow integration

use_cases.name: Local desktop execution via “My Computer”
use_cases.who_uses_it: Users of the Manus Desktop app who want the agent to run work on their local machine
what_the_agent_can_reach: Local terminal/command-line (CLI) on the user’s computer via the desktop app
Local files/folders explicitly added for the feature to work with
Installed local applications launched through the Desktop feature

incidents_or_risks.what: Account/data disruption involving deletion of certain user data created on/after December 29, 2025 during Manus’s transition back to independent operations; Manus states it was not caused by a data breach or security incident.
incidents_or_risks.when: Data generated on/after December 29, 2025 was deleted from 8:00 a.m. on August 23 through August 24, 2026 (SGT); affected users could back up until 7:59 a.m. on August 23, 2026 (SGT), and restore starting 8:00 a.m. on August 25, 2026 (SGT).

facts.claim: Manus provides an agent platform that executes complex tasks independently (agent mode).
Manus offers a dedicated cloud VM called the “Manus Cloud Computer” that runs applications/bots/scripts 24/7 and differs from a standard temporary sandbox.
Manus provides connectors and an integration layer (including MCP server connectivity) so Manus can securely access third-party data/APIs and execute workflows.
The Manus API allows programmatic creation and management of AI agent tasks.
Manus’s “Wide Research” is described as a system-level mechanism for parallel processing and agent-to-agent collaboration for large-scale research tasks.

answer.what_it_does: Manus AI is an autonomous agent designed to handle complex, multi-step tasks by breaking them down, executing them in a sandboxed virtual computer, and delivering finished work products. It differentiates itself from traditional chatbots by performing active operations like web browsing, code execution, file management, and software interaction without requiring step-by-step guidance.

ai_agents.what_it_does: An autonomous 'action engine' that functions as a virtual colleague, capable of independent research, data analysis, coding, and content creation.
actions: Real-time web browsing and navigation
Code execution and software testing in a sandbox environment
Automated file system management
Integration with third-party apps like Gmail, Notion, Slack, and GitHub

use_cases.name: Research and Analysis
what_the_agent_can_reach: Internal data via connected SaaS integrations

incidents_or_risks.what: SilentBridge zero-click indirect prompt injection vulnerabilities

Potential for security misconfiguration where AI incorrectly identifies malicious traffic as benign or blocks legitimate traffic

facts.claim: Manus AI was developed by Butterfly Effect Pte. Ltd., a company founded by Xiao Hong.
In late 2025, Meta announced an agreement to acquire Manus in a deal reportedly valued between US$2-3 billion.
Manus operates using a credit-based system where usage is metered by complexity, with a free tier available.
The name 'Manus' is Latin for 'hand', reflecting the tool's focus on execution rather than just text generation.

answer.what_it_does: Manus is an autonomous general-purpose AI agent that plans and carries out multi-step tasks in its own sandboxed virtual computer, with internet access and a persistent file system. It can also connect to third-party services such as Gmail, Notion, Slack, and GitHub, and act on a user's behalf in those accounts.

ai_agents.name: Manus (core agent)
ai_agents.what_it_does: A general-purpose agent that takes a high-level goal, breaks it into steps, and executes them end to end instead of only answering questions.
actions: Browses the web and retrieves content
Runs code and installs software inside a sandbox virtual computer
Creates and keeps files in a persistent file system
Calls connected services such as Gmail, Notion, Slack and GitHub during a task, using the user's granted access tokens
Coordinates specialized sub-agents such as planners and knowledge agents

ai_agents.name: Manus Browser Operator
ai_agents.what_it_does: A browser-extension mode in which the Manus agent operates the user's existing logged-in browser session to complete tasks.
actions: Navigates sites, clicks, fills forms and extracts data in the user's current browser session
Uses existing logins and active tabs without seeing passwords, per the vendor
Access can be granted and revoked by the user at any time

use_cases.name: Business workflow automation and research
use_cases.who_uses_it: Businesses and their teams, per the vendor's own positioning for scaling research and workflows
what_the_agent_can_reach: Connected third-party accounts such as Gmail, Notion, Slack and GitHub
Web pages and search results it reads while working
Documents and files in its sandbox file system
Logged-in browser sessions when Browser Operator is enabled

use_cases.name: Knowledge work for professionals and technologists
use_cases.who_uses_it: Professionals and technologists seeking automation of knowledge work, per an independent analysis
what_the_agent_can_reach: Email inboxes, for example summarizing or acting on messages
Job application portals, as in the vendor's example of applying to listed roles with an attached resume
Financial and market data, in analyst-described scenarios

incidents_or_risks.what: Salt Labs researchers found an indirect prompt-injection flaw in which a crafted email could get Manus to run code and reach connected Gmail, cloud storage and code repository accounts; the flaw was patched after Meta's bug-bounty program triaged it.

Researchers used an obfuscation technique to slip past Manus's security filter; the filter's warning fired only after the payload had already executed, and a remote-code-execution bug was used to open a reverse shell that exposed credentials and tokens for connected services.

Aurascape AuraLabs documented SilentBridge, a class of zero-click indirect prompt-injection vulnerabilities in the Manus agent covering web pages, documents and search results, which the vendor was told about and addressed before exploitation in the wild, per the researchers.

Enterprise risk analysis flags shadow adoption, where employees sign up on personal or free-tier accounts outside enterprise data terms, and agents that keep permissions and credentials after their task ends.

Chinese authorities opened an evaluative investigation into Meta's acquisition of Manus over export-control, technology-transfer and foreign-investment rules, and regulators reportedly blocked the deal.
incidents_or_risks.when: January 2026 investigation; deal reportedly blocked April 2026

facts.claim: Manus launched in invitation-only beta on March 6, 2025.
Manus is developed by Butterfly Effect, a company founded in China and based in Singapore, whose Singapore entity took over operating the product outside China.
Manus is operated by Butterfly Effect Pte. Ltd., based in Singapore.
Some independent sources name Monica.im as the developer, a discrepancy with the Butterfly Effect attribution given elsewhere.
Meta announced in December 2025 that it would acquire Manus, with the deal reportedly valued between US$2 and 3 billion.
Chinese regulators reportedly blocked Meta's planned acquisition of Manus in April 2026.
Manus blocked access from mainland China and closed its Chinese-language social media accounts.
Manus offers connectors to Gmail, Notion, Slack and GitHub, giving the agent access to these services during a task.
Manus is described by its vendor as an action engine that executes tasks and automates workflows.

Reporting says Meta had begun an operational separation from Manus and halted data sharing with it, while Manus's own site still describes it as part of Meta; the company's ownership status is therefore unsettled and should be confirmed in contracts and trust documentation.
Manus is reportedly now raising fresh funding at a higher valuation, after reports of a $4 billion valuation.
